about: Language-neutral conformance cases for wiggle's placement rules: the instance-id format, and
the decisions that map an id to the cell holding it.
Java, Go and Python each implement these, so each can drift. This file is the shared answer.
Vendor it beside the .proto files and run it in each client's test suite.
Numbers are integers. 'cell': null means the id carries no cell label, which is not an error --
it means 'ask the ring', the behaviour of every id minted before labels existed.

format.name: namespace, cell, epoch, shard and ulid
no cell omits the segment -- the pre-label format, unchanged
a blank cell omits it too, rather than minting an empty segment
a namespace with a dot is rejected -- it is the first segment
a cell with a dot is rejected for the same reason
an id longer than a storage column is refused at mint, not at insert

parse.name: an unlabelled id parses with a null cell -- not an error
a ulid beginning with 'c' and containing a dot is NOT a cell segment
parse.why: the label sits before the epoch precisely so this cannot be misread

parse.name: a bare wfi_ id is legacy
a non-numeric epoch is legacy, not an error

resolve.name: a shard beyond the ring wraps into it, so no id is unroutable
an id keeps resolving through ITS epoch after a reshard moved its shard
resolve.why: shard 1 belongs to cell-b at epoch 1, but this instance was written at epoch 0

resolve.name: a new id on the same shard goes to the new owner
the label wins over the ring when its cell is live
resolve.why: the ring says where a shard belongs; the label says where the instance was written

resolve.name: a label whose cell has no live nodes falls back to the ring
a label agreeing with the ring changes nothing
an unplaced namespace resolves to nothing
an epoch with no ring resolves to nothing
a retired epoch still resolves -- retired is about work, not addressing

mintable.name: a cell the current ring names may mint its own shards
a ring that excludes the cell puts it on standby
an unplaced namespace is not standby -- nobody decided anything
a cell also named by a draining epoch still mints into the current one
after a reshard the new owner mints its shard
a cell only in a retired epoch mints nothing
a cell owning shards in a current epoch that is not open mints nothing
mintable.why: no correct writer leaves a policy like this -- but it is read from a shared store, so a peer running older or wrong code can, and minting into a draining epoch must be refused rather than assumed impossible
